title: Timeouts retries and cancellation
outcome: Explain timeouts retries and cancellation using the deciding step in this fictional service.
scenario: Retry within declared limits. A read-only lookup allows two attempts of at most one second each. Cancellation forbids further attempts.
given: First attempt times out at 1 second. Second succeeds in 0.4 seconds. Ignore overhead. No cancellation occurs.

steps.label: Bound first wait
steps.detail: Stop attempt one after its one-second allowance.

steps.label: Check retry
steps.detail: One attempt remains, and cancellation has not occurred.

steps.label: Complete next attempt
steps.detail: Accept the checked record; total waiting is 1.4 seconds.

explanation: A timeout bounds waiting; a retry tries again; cancellation withdraws the request. They are separate conditions on the next action.

counterfactual.change: Cancellation arrives after the first timeout.
counterfactual.prediction: Do not start the second attempt.
counterfactual.reason: Cancellation overrides the unused retry allowance.

student_task: Calculate waiting time for a one-second timeout followed by a 0.4-second success. What changes if cancellation arrives after the first attempt but before the retry?
teacher_answer: Stop attempt one after its one-second allowance. One attempt remains, and cancellation has not occurred. Accept the checked record; total waiting is 1.4 seconds. Changed case: Do not start the second attempt. Cancellation overrides the unused retry allowance.
project_evidence: For the Grounded Learning Service, retain an annotated trace and the changed-case result. Name the contract or evidence that makes the deciding step valid, so another team can review it.
limits: The arithmetic excludes overhead; retries of side-effecting operations require separate duplicate and recovery controls.
review_note: Individually authored fictional practice, distinct from the reserved independent case. These stipulated records illustrate reasoning; no real service execution or learner outcome is claimed.
